name: BACH_0099_FSIM_blur3
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (62%)** · Ambiguous: InSitu vs Invasive · Careful review
Invasive holds 38% and sits in the 90% conformal set [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 62%, Invasive 38% | Two-class split |
| Conformal set | InSitu, Invasive (90%) | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.96 / 1.0 | No reliability flag |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes | Same top class as UNI2-h |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 InSitu [F5] | Three neighbors Invasive |

## Tissue evidence
- **Scarce benign stroma or fat** (region 0) · ↑ invasive · Low score is associated with invasive in the concept model [F3] · Validated
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 2, 6, 9) · ↑ invasive · High score, but spot check was poor · Unreliable
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 3) · ↓ invasive · Score below typical, lowering invasive association · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (region 9) · ↓ invasive · Score below typical · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined to ducts** (region 5) · ↓ invasive · Score above typical; fits in situ pattern · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so not shown to reflect the classifier. Necrosis (3/20) and normal lobules (0/20) are Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Blur severity 3 may hide stromal invasion; reliability score only modestly flags errors (AUROC 0.69).
- Necrosis, if real, would raise invasive likelihood.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 7, 3, 11**: highest heatmap contribution toward invasive; look for stromal invasion.
2. **Regions 2, 6, 9**: confirm whether necrosis is real; its spot check was poor.
3. **Region 5**: separate duct-confined cells from stromal invasion.
